differences: Cohen's d for the change of the hand-switch cost from 1 to 3 irrelevant movements is reported as 0.59 and for the short vs long delay as -0.03; the shared data give 0.56 and -0.02 (t = 2.75 and -0.11, df and p reproduce).
The abstract's N = 65 counts everyone recruited (22, 26 and 17); the files hold the 58 analysed participants (20, 24 and 14).

The Methods give 40 trials per block for Exp. 2; the shared file has three blocks of up to 32 trials (96 per participant, as the deposit README says). The README also says 26 trials per block for Exp. 1 and 32 for Exp. 3 and codes the visuospatial set size 0 or 1; the files have blocks of 24 (Exp. 1) and 48, 48 and 24 (Exp. 3, as in the Methods) and set sizes 1 and 3.

The files lack 54 of 1920 scheduled trials in Exp. 1 (2.8%) and 103 of 2304 in Exp. 2 (4.5%); the Methods report 2.0% and 4.4% timeouts plus lapses (1.58% and 1.48% in Exp. 1, 2.35% in Exp. 2, 2.27% in Exp. 3), which add up to more, so the reported rates cannot be matched to the missing trials. All shared errors lie inside the lapse cutoffs, so the lapses were removed before sharing; trials after a block's last shared trial cannot be told from trials not run, so no placeholders are added there (1, 6 and 15 trial numbers in Exp. 1, 2 and 3).
The text gives the Exp. 1 correlation between mean Euclidean error and dispersion as 0.99; the shared data give 0.9988.
